question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-|2x-5| & =3 \\ -|2x-5| & =-1 \\ |2x-5| & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following two cases:

- If $|2x-5|=2x-5,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2x-5| & =1 \\ 2x-5 & =1 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|2x-5|=-(2x-5),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2x-5| & =1 \\ -(2x-5) & =1 \\ -2x+5 & =1 \\ -2x & =-4 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $x=2$ and $x=3.$
